summary: Open tower in Sullivan County NH, listed gone; a 2015 forum post puts it on an unnamed peak in Pillsbury State Park.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association. The latest description of the summit is a 2015 forum post.

access.note: The summit is said to lie in Pillsbury State Park (2015 forum post), which is a state park. No source describes access to the summit today.

events.note: A 2015 visit reported eyebolts, cable and a fireplace on the summit, with almost no view. This records remains, not a lookout event.

resolved_conflicts.field: position of the tower within the park
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2015 post places the tower on an unnamed peak in the park, with no compass direction given. A later forum comment doubts the list's accuracy and says the tower was south of the main park, not north. The story reports that comment and does not choose a side.

notes_for_editor: No fetched source gives a build date, builder, design height, staffing or fire record. The FFLA detail page (firelookout.org/lookouts/nh/pillsbury.htm) returns 404. A search snippet described a 1934 temporary tower and a 1923 patrol, but it could not be quoted from a fetched page, so the story omits it. The link between the name Pillsbury Reservation and Pillsbury State Park rests only on the 2015 forum post, not an official source. The listing coordinates (43.27658, -72.07272) lie northeast of the park's Wikipedia centre (43.23083, -72.09972); not checked on a map. Kind correction: the brief says platform, FFLA says Open Tower. Worth checking the NH Division of Forests and Lands and Baird and Haartz, Field Guide to New Hampshire Firetowers (not read).
